basic.name: Sandra Chaparro
basic.summary: I bring real software engineering and application-security experience into my transition into cybersecurity.
basic.about: I'm a software engineer based in the Dallas–Fort Worth area. My path started in Computer Science, moved into full-stack software engineering, and has run through production systems ever since — healthcare EHR platforms, internal dashboards, and client web products. That production work kept putting real security problems in front of me: authenticating users, authorizing access, and protecting sensitive data. Cybersecurity is the next deliberate step on that same path, not a restart — I'm building focused knowledge in threat intelligence, OSINT, threat hunting, and AI security through certification study and self-directed learning, on top of the application-security experience I already have. I care about technology that actually helps people, and I bring a developer's instincts to security problems: curious, detail-oriented, and always growing.

securityJourney.narrative: My move into cybersecurity isn't a cold start — production engineering kept putting real security work in front of me: protecting patient data, securing APIs, and completing federal compliance training. This is a continuation of that work, not a departure from it.
applied: Implemented authentication and authorization middleware protecting sensitive patient data in a production healthcare EHR.
Built JWT-based authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) to safeguard protected health information (PHI).
Completed FedRAMP compliance training covering security controls, authorization requirements, and best practices for federal data.
learning: Studying for the CISSP certification (ISC2) — in progress.
Studying for CompTIA Security+ — in progress.
Applying security-first practices in day-to-day development work while building toward threat intelligence, OSINT, threat hunting, and AI security.
